# BTCDecoded Intelligence

> Cited search over Bitcoin’s public development record. Not a live price desk. Not on-chain analytics.

Pay with Lightning. Connect over MCP. Cite the record before citing analysis.

## Connect

- Endpoint: `https://mcp.btcdecoded.org/mcp` (streamable HTTP)
- Sign in: GitHub or Nostr at https://btcdecoded.org/account/
- Pay: Lightning at https://btcdecoded.org/subscribe/ — key stays on that account
- Claude: OAuth custom connector. Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector. Paste name, MCP URL, client ID, and client secret from Account. After Connect, sign in on mcp.btcdecoded.org if asked, then Allow
- Cursor and raw HTTP: Bearer key from Account (Claude does not use this key)
- Site index: https://btcdecoded.org/llms.txt

## Plans

Every plan searches both layers. Same key on upgrade (sat difference only).

- Trial: 15,000 sats, 7 days, 20 queries/day
- Researcher: 50,000 / 128,000 / 240,000 / 456,000 sats for 30 / 90 / 180 / 365 days, 100 queries/day
- Developer: 100,000 / 255,000 / 480,000 / 913,000 sats for 30 / 90 / 180 / 365 days, 500 queries/day, plus `analyze_pr` on allowlisted public PRs (Bitcoin Core and BLVM)

Human pages: [Plans](https://btcdecoded.org/pricing/), [Checkout](https://btcdecoded.org/subscribe/), [Account](https://btcdecoded.org/account/).

## Layers

- curated (~19k): specs, maps, findings, project docs, research writeups, open textbooks
- record (~684k): contemporaneous public sources
- price: CoinMetrics community PriceUSD, every daily close from 2010-07-18 through the last dated row (ISO-week passages)
- total nearly 700k passages (19,483 + 683,718 ingest)

## Full record (~684k)

- GitHub: PRs, issues, commits, merged-by map
- bitcoin-dev and cryptography mailing lists
- Delving Bitcoin posts and topics
- Satoshi communications archive
- BIP texts, BIP PRs and issues
- Release tags and signers
- Bitcoin Core source: consensus, policy, script, validation, net, mempool, miner
- Bitcointalk forum posts (~159k)
- IRC review channel logs (~371k)
- Historical BTC/USD every daily close (CoinMetrics PriceUSD, 2010-07-18–)

## Curated (~19k)

- Research findings and data
- Canonical maintainer data
- Training corpus: Bitcoin domain, epistemology, ops files, discourse games, argument map
- Bitcoin Commons book chapters
- Select articles (`source=articles`): Wei Dai, b-money (November 1998, http://www.weidai.com/bmoney.txt); Adam Back, Hashcash (1 August 2002, http://www.hashcash.org/papers/hashcash.pdf); Hal Finney, RPOW (15 August 2004, https://nakamotoinstitute.org/library/rpow/); Nick Szabo, Bit gold (29 December 2005, https://nakamotoinstitute.org/library/bit-gold/); Joseph Poon and Thaddeus Dryja, The Bitcoin Lightning Network (14 January 2016 draft 0.5.9.2, https://lightning.network/lightning-network-paper.pdf)
- Open textbooks (`source=textbooks`): Learning Bitcoin from the Command Line (Allen/Appelcline/Blockchain Commons, CC BY 4.0, v2.2.2); Bitcoin Programming Textbook (Karasavvas, CC BY-SA 4.0); Bitcoin Developer Reference (minium, CC BY-SA 4.0); Elementary Bitcoin (Carvalho, CC BY-SA 4.0); Programming the Blockchain in C# (Dorier, CC BY-SA 3.0); Book of Bitcoin preface and commentary (asherp, CC BY 4.0 — not chain-rendered pages); Mastering Bitcoin 2nd ed print 3 (Antonopoulos, CC BY-SA 4.0); Mastering Bitcoin 3rd ed (Antonopoulos/Harding, CC BY-SA 4.0); Mastering the Lightning Network 1st ed (Antonopoulos/Osuntokun/Pickhardt, CC BY-SA 4.0); Lightning BOLTs (CC BY 4.0); Mastering Taproot (Zhang, CC BY-SA 4.0); bitcoin.org developer docs including RPC reference (MIT); Bitcoin Optech English topics and newsletters (public domain per Optech README)
- BLVM spec and Orange Paper pointer
- BLVM docs
- Bitcoin Commons whitepaper
- Bitcoin whitepaper
- Commons ecosystem vision
- Commons Pool docs
- Review intelligence and expectations

## Roles

- source: cite as evidence (record dumps; named precursor papers under `source=articles` with author, date, URL)
- spec: cite as canonical text (whitepaper, Orange Paper, BLVM spec, BIP text)
- analysis: findings, maps, Commons book, argument map, open textbooks — label as analysis / textbook
- product: BLVM / Commons / Pool docs
- internal: training, epistemology, ops, discourse games, review expectations — do not cite as history

## Behavior

- Hits include role, source, document, and date when known.
- Unpinned mix: lead (spec / whitepapers / articles) then contemporaneous record, then labeled analysis (cap 3). Price only if pinned or the query landed on price. Spec/articles are queried on their own so Optech cannot hide them. IRC is capped in the record band when GitHub/mail/BIP hits exist.
- GitHub PRs/issues/commits, bitcoin-dev mail, Core `src/` paths, BIP PRs/issues, Delving dump URLs, Core release tags, and `Source:` headers include an openable URL when the dump id, metadata, or excerpt is enough to build one.
- Empty if the index has no passage.
- If source/spec and analysis conflict, return the source/spec and label the analysis.
- Lightning is how you pay, not part of the corpus.
- MCP is the product interface, not a corpus source.

## Out of scope

Live spot, ETF flows, derivatives, chain analytics, wallet tracing, private chat, unpublished meetings.

## Producer

BTCDecoded / Bitcoin Commons. Maps and findings are analysis. Named precursor papers are source texts. Open textbooks are instructional, not the record.
